statement_en: That this project can DESIGN an organism, operationalised as: the designed "winged zebrafish" is measurably close to a real flying fish on the ten pre-registered axes.
reason_detail: The attempt failed not because the design scored badly but because 9 of the 10 pre-registered axes could not be scored at all, and the defining axis fails on BOTH sides: no fetched source gives an adult zebrafish pectoral fin length / SL, and the design side exists only inside a figure the thread refused to digitise. The one scoreable axis (body mass vs SL exponent) put the design on the zebrafish and none of the way to the flying fish. The constraint gate did not discriminate either: the real flying fish also fails it, by a factor of 29 on E3.
what_was_tried: Pre-registration of the ten axes and the decision rules BEFORE any number was produced (design-validation/PREREG.md, sha256 ea6f99eb25b48cdba85d2766b20bc4d8797dfa243c7c6dc784ef2815b72aaa76, hashed 2026-10-31T22:00:34Z).
Scoring the design against the ten morphological axes: 1 of 10 scored, 9 of 10 could not be scored.

A genetic overlap count against the loci known to differ in flying fishes: 1 of 74 (1.4%), and the 74 is coding-only because sheets K and M carry no gene column, so the true denominator is larger by an unknown amount.
Running the Lean constraint gate on the design: 18 of 21 constraints could not be evaluated, and the real flying fish fails the gate too.
Taking the HARSHER pre-registered consequence was considered and rejected as overstating what the gate can tell us; PREREG rule 2 (drop as unsupported) was applied instead of rule 1 (drop outright).
what_survives: The method survives and so does the finding. Pre-registering the axes is what made the result legible: the count of UNSCOREABLE parameters became the headline rather than a quiet omission, and the gate's failure to separate the design from the real animal was caught rather than reported as a pass. The durable scientific finding is that the design's phenotypic claim was never this project's to validate -- it is Daane et al. 2021's own published double heterozygote -- and that the single measurement which would let anyone score it, the pectoral fin length of that fish, has never been published as a number. The 1-of-74 genetic overlap stands as a real, if small, number, and the one convergent locus is a genuine hit.
sources: Daane JM et al. 2021, Curr Biol, PMID 34534441, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054

evidence.claim: The headline failure, in the report's own words.
evidence.quote: **On the axis the whole design is about we cannot say how close it is, because the measurement exists only inside a figure we refused to digitise; the one morphological axis that can be scored puts the design exactly on the zebrafish and none of the way to the flying fish; and genetically the design reproduces 1 of the 74 loci known to differ in flying fishes (1.4 %), that one being a real convergent hit on `lat4a`/`slc43a2a` while the other half of the design is a gene with no flying-fish evidence at all.**

evidence.claim: The gate does not discriminate, which is a finding about the gate.
evidence.quote: **The real flying fish also FAILS the gate**, by a factor of 29 on E3. "FAILS" does not separate the design from the target.
evidence.kind: negative control on the constraint gate

evidence.claim: The honest ruling, and the refusal to take the harsher option the pre-registration allowed.
evidence.quote: The claim that we can DESIGN an organism is not supported by this validation, and the reason is not that the design scored badly: it is that the design is not measurable on the axes that define it, and the one genetic number that can be computed (1/74) says the design reproduces a single convergent locus out of everything known to differ. Dropping the claim outright under rule 1 overstates what this gate can tell us; the honest position is PREREG rule 2, drop the claim as UNSUPPORTED.

found_by: Published by the design-validation thread as a failure, in full, with its pre-registration hash. Harvested here so the failure is a first-class registry object rather than a report nobody queries.

history.change: harvested by the open-questions thread from the thread that published the failure

scope_note: Static mirror of lean/registry/open-questions/. An OPEN QUESTION is a question this project holds unsettled, with an arm per live position, each arm's evidence quoted from its primary source, and a belief `proportion` COMPUTED by pipeline/leanbio/belief.mjs rather than asserted. A proportion orders the arms; it is NOT a probability that an arm is true, and belief-params.json says plainly that its parameters are hand-set and not fitted. No arm of an open question is in any law set, and the guard in openq-lib.mjs refuses to accept a law that asserts one. A FAILED THEOREM is a statement this project tried and could not establish, kept with its reason so nobody reproposes it; `what_survives` says what is still true after the failure. READ `attempted`: a failed-theorem record with `attempted: false` was NEVER TRIED (the single Lean build lock was contended, or it was abandoned on cost, or withheld on purpose), so it is not a result about the statement at all and its `proof_status` says so; the counts report attempted and never-attempted separately for that reason. A NOT-CHECKABLE-IN-PRINCIPLE record is a fourth thing: sound, usually proved, but with no falsifiable direction over any design, so NO input would make it bind -- it carries no `missing_inputs`, because a list of them would read as a to-do and misstate the finding. Arms formalised in Lean are proved internally consistent and are NOT proved true of any organism.
